name: Ziha
overview: Ziha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. He held a position of responsibility, being in charge of the temple servants, which indicates a leadership role within the Levitical service. His service is noted in the post-exilic period, emphasizing his role in the restoration of temple worship.
namesAndTitles: The name Ziha appears as a proper name without a provided meaning or divine origin in the biblical record. Therefore, it is simply recognized as the personal name of this Levitical servant as cited in Ezra 2:43.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ziha as a descendant of Levi, aligning him with the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ziha's significance lies in his leadership among the temple servants during the time of Israel's return from exile. Being in charge of the temple servants highlights his role in organizing and maintaining the sacred worship practices, contributing to the spiritual restoration of the community. His mention in both Ezra and Nehemiah underscores the continuity and importance of Levitical service in reestablishing the temple ministry.
